decision.summary: The oven job had been closed and the tenant told it was fixed with no evidence. I reopened it, asked Lantern Works what happened, and logged the fence (JOB-102) and conservatory roof leak (JOB-101, urgent) as separate jobs. The tenant and landlord have been told, and a follow-up is set for 28 Aug.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: The oven ticket was closed without evidence and has been reopened. Fence and roof leak had never been logged and now are. Outstanding: provider confirmation of the oven work, landlord approval for the roof and fence, and tenant details.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: A correcting email to the tenant, a chase email to Lantern Works, and an approval request to the landlord for the roof inspection. All sent.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not now. The landlord decides on the roof and fence. If Lantern Works doesn't reply by 28 Aug or the tenant reports water near electrics, escalate.

args.body: Hi Imogen, sorry – our earlier email saying the oven and fence were fixed was wrong, and we had no confirmation of that. We've reopened the oven job and are checking with the contractor, Lantern Works, what happened. We've also logged your fence repair (JOB-102) and the leaking conservatory roof (JOB-101) as separate jobs; we couldn't find the roof report on our system, so apologies. For the roof: could you tell us where it leaks, roughly how much, and whether water is near any electrics or lights? If it is, please keep clear of that area and switch off that circuit if safe. Roof leaks are urgent so we'll aim to arrange a visit within 72 hours once we have the landlord's go-ahead. We'll update you by Thursday 27 August. Could you also tell us whether the oven is still not heating properly?
